comments.author: @kelvinnaholo8234
comments.text:
I'm from Namibia 🇳🇦 and much of the world at large have a wrong perception of the country. Please people of the world 🌎, Namibia is not a desert. It has two deserts on the East and West. 

Yes much of central and southern of the country are arid but not deserts. 

We have different ecosystems including thick forests where the Chinese have been harvesting timber load into ships 🚢 to China 🇨🇳. Certainly a desert 🏜 can't produce harvestable timber. There're many people in Namibia 🇳🇦 who have no slightest idea of what a desert is. People of Eastern Ohangwena region, Kavango West & East as well as Zambezi region feel awkward when they hear of their places being called a desert.

Those asking about water, greater part of Namibia 🇳🇦 has no water problems. Namibia has massive underground water💧aquifers such as in Ohangwena region that can last its people even it were to boom to a population of a million people for 600-900 years without a single drop of rain 🌧. Boreholes have been drilled across the country to supply rural people with clean drinking water. 

In our towns and cities our taps don't run dry. We don't experience water outages unless there's work on a pipe and residents are notified right before hand to prepare for the disruption which hardly goes for a whole day.

And to the content creators be informative per excellence because some of the scenes and statistics in this documentary aren't from Namibia. For example for employment and unemployment stats you showed Zambia 🇿🇲 not Namibia. Travel the whole country not just the desert and form a balanced picture.

Thanks for the documentary but it must be a true reflection.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: No one is denying that Namibia has major desert regions. 😄 The point is simply that the entire country is not one continuous desert. Namibia also has savannas, woodlands, wetlands, towns, farmland, and very different ecosystems depending on the region. Showing that diversity isn’t “justifying” anything, it’s giving a more complete picture of the country. 🇳🇦

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text:
Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed perspective, especially as someone from Namibia. 🇳🇦🙏 You make an important point: Namibia should never be reduced to one giant desert. The country has very different landscapes, ecosystems, towns, farming areas, and ways of life that deserve to be represented too.
I also really appreciate you correcting the impression we gave about water access and pointing out that some of the footage and statistics did not accurately reflect Namibia. That is fair criticism. A documentary about a country should give viewers a balanced and authentic picture, not let one dramatic landscape define the entire nation.
Thank you for still watching and for helping us understand Namibia better from a local point of view. We'll take the seriously and be much more careful with our research, statistics, and location-specific visuals going forward. ❤️

comments.text: I swear by God that I only speak out because of hunger, poverty, and dire circumstances. My younger siblings and I have gone three days without food. Every hour, our landlord knocks, demanding rent and threatening to throw us out onto the street if we do not pay. O people with compassionate hearts—I swear by the One who raised the heavens and spread out the earth—there is not even a single day’s worth of food in our home; we are suffering immensely, relying only on the occasional help of neighbors. You who love your own sons and daughters—please know that we, too, are someone’s daughters, and we, are suffering in agony, yet no one looks upon us with a merciful eye.... I appeal to you, those who love to do good:,,,.we are orphans with no one to turn to, and we face the threat of being evicted from our home and cast out onto the street if we do not pay the rent.,.,.😊😊🎉😢😢😊😢😊

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: I'm truly sorry to hear what you and your younger siblings are going through. No family should have to face days without food while also worrying about losing their home. Thank you for having the courage to share your situation here. I sincerely hope someone in your local community who is able to help sees your message, and that better days come for you and your family very soon. Sending you a big hug, strength, and all our warmest wishes from the channel. ❤️🙏
